metadata.title: iGCSE Computing: Hardware
metadata.selection_note: Curated to the 50 strongest hardware-focused terms from the supplied list.

questions.definition: A component in a computer system that processes data and instructions.
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches, decodes, and executes instructions. It contains components such as the ALU, control unit, and registers.

questions.definition: The component in the CPU that performs mathematical and logical operations.
questions.explanation: The ALU performs calculations such as addition and logic operations such as comparisons.

questions.definition: The component in the CPU that controls all operations in the CPU.
questions.explanation: The control unit decodes instructions and sends control signals to coordinate the fetch-decode-execute cycle.

questions.definition: The part of the CPU that contains the components used to perform the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
questions.clue: A CPU may contain more than one.
questions.explanation: Each core can process instructions. More cores can improve performance when software can use them effectively.

questions.definition: The number of fetch-decode-execute cycles that can be performed in a second.
questions.explanation: Higher clock speed can increase the number of instructions processed per second, though it is not the only factor affecting performance.

questions.definition: A type of storage built into or close to the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions.
questions.explanation: Cache reduces the time the CPU waits for data by keeping frequently used instructions and data nearby.

questions.definition: A small component in a computer system used to temporarily store data.
questions.clue: Very fast storage inside the CPU.
questions.explanation: Registers hold small amounts of data, addresses, or instructions needed immediately by the CPU.

questions.definition: A register built into the ALU that stores the result of interim calculations.
questions.explanation: The accumulator temporarily stores results while the ALU carries out arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.definition: A CPU register that stores the address of the next instruction to be processed.
questions.explanation: The program counter helps the CPU fetch instructions in the correct order.

questions.definition: A CPU register that stores the address of the next instruction or data to be accessed.
questions.explanation: The MAR stores the memory location that the CPU wants to read from or write to.

questions.definition: A CPU register that holds data or instructions fetched from RAM.
questions.clue: Holds data moving to or from memory.
questions.explanation: The MDR temporarily stores data or instructions being transferred between the CPU and memory.

questions.definition: A register built into the control unit that holds the current instruction being processed.
questions.explanation: The CIR holds the instruction currently being decoded or executed by the CPU.

questions.definition: The cycle through which data and instructions are processed.
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, and then executes it.

questions.definition: A set of commands that can be processed by a certain CPU.
questions.explanation: The instruction set defines the operations a CPU can decode and execute.

questions.definition: Wires used for the transmission of addresses between components in a computer.
questions.explanation: The address bus carries the address of the memory location the CPU wants to access.

questions.definition: Wires used for the transmission of data and instructions between components in a computer.
questions.explanation: The data bus transfers data and instructions between the CPU, memory, and other components.

questions.definition: Wires used for the transmission of control signals between components in a computer.
questions.explanation: The control bus carries signals such as read, write, and timing signals to coordinate components.

questions.definition: The design of a computer system, including the components it contains.
questions.clue: The structure of a computer system.
questions.explanation: Computer architecture describes how components such as the CPU, memory, buses, and input/output devices are organised.

questions.definition: An integrated circuit that is able to perform many of the functions of a CPU.
questions.explanation: A microprocessor contains processing circuitry on a chip and is used in computers and embedded systems.

questions.definition: A computer system that performs a dedicated function.
questions.explanation: Embedded systems are found in devices such as washing machines, traffic lights, vehicles, and appliances.

questions.definition: The connection of computer systems and everyday devices using the internet to allow data to be exchanged.
questions.explanation: IoT devices collect and exchange data, such as smart thermostats, fitness trackers, and connected appliances.

questions.definition: A component that holds data and programs currently in use.
questions.explanation: RAM is fast temporary memory. Its contents are lost when the computer is switched off.

questions.definition: A type of primary storage that stores the start-up instructions for the computer.
questions.explanation: ROM keeps its contents without power and often stores firmware or boot instructions.

questions.definition: A type of storage that is directly accessed by the CPU.
questions.explanation: Primary storage is used by the CPU for data and instructions needed while the computer runs.

questions.definition: A type of storage designed to store data permanently until it is deleted by the user.
questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile and includes magnetic, optical, and solid-state storage.

questions.definition: A type of secondary storage that uses magnetism to store data.
questions.clue: Hard disk drives are an example.
questions.explanation: Magnetic storage records data by magnetising areas of a disk or tape.

questions.definition: A type of secondary storage that uses lasers to store data.
questions.explanation: Optical storage uses laser light to read marks on a disc surface.

questions.definition: A type of secondary storage that uses transistors to store data.
questions.clue: SSDs and flash drives use this.
questions.explanation: Solid-state storage has no moving parts and stores data using electronic circuits.

questions.definition: A type of memory that can be used as an extension to RAM.
questions.clue: Uses secondary storage when RAM is full.
questions.explanation: Virtual memory lets a system continue running when RAM is limited, but it is slower than RAM.

questions.definition: Data storage owned by a third party and accessed by the user using the internet.
questions.explanation: Cloud storage stores data on remote servers and allows access from different devices through the internet.

questions.definition: A device that allows data to be entered into a computer system.
questions.explanation: Input devices provide data or commands for the computer to process.

questions.definition: A device that can be used to obtain the results of processed data.
questions.explanation: Output devices present information from the computer to the user, such as images, sound, or printed text.

questions.definition: A type of input device used to capture data from its immediate environment.
questions.explanation: Sensors measure physical conditions such as light, temperature, pressure, sound, or movement.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the temperature of an object, substance, or surrounding environment.
questions.explanation: Temperature sensors are used in heating systems, weather stations, engines, and medical devices.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the force of pressure applied to the sensor or device.
questions.clue: Measures pressure from solids, liquids, or gases.
questions.explanation: Pressure sensors are used in tyres, weather systems, industrial machinery, and medical devices.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures ambient light or direct light.
questions.explanation: Light sensors are used in automatic lighting, cameras, and phones that adjust screen brightness.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures infra-red radiation emitted by objects or people.
questions.explanation: Infra-red sensors are used in remote controls, motion detectors, and thermal sensing.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures how close an object is in comparison to the sensor.
questions.explanation: Proximity sensors can detect objects without contact by emitting a field or radiation and measuring its return.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures acceleration forces, including gravity, movement, and vibrations.
questions.explanation: Accelerometers are used in phones, vehicles, and game controllers to detect movement and orientation.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the level of sound in an environment.
questions.explanation: Acoustic sensors can monitor noise levels or detect specific sounds.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the level of moisture in the immediate atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Humidity sensors are used in weather stations, greenhouses, and climate control systems.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the amount of water present in a substance, such as soil.
questions.explanation: Moisture sensors can help automate watering systems by checking how wet soil is.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the presence and concentration of a gas in the immediate atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Gas sensors can be used for safety systems, pollution monitoring, or industrial control.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the amount of liquid, gas, or steam flowing through or around an environment.
questions.explanation: Flow sensors are used in pipes, heating systems, and industrial processes.

questions.definition: A sensor that measures the pH level of a substance.
questions.explanation: pH sensors are used in laboratories, agriculture, water testing, and industrial processes.

questions.definition: The component in a computer that is used to connect it to a network.
questions.clue: Network hardware inside or attached to a device.
questions.explanation: A NIC allows a device to communicate over a wired or wireless network.

questions.definition: A unique address given to a computer or network interface at the manufacturing stage.
questions.explanation: A MAC address identifies a network interface and is usually assigned by the manufacturer.

questions.definition: A component that acts as a central resource for storing data, applications, or providing a service.
questions.explanation: Servers can provide files, websites, email, authentication, or application services to other devices.

questions.definition: A network component that examines a data packet to obtain its destination address and forwards it to that address.
questions.explanation: Routers move data between networks and help packets reach their destination.

questions.definition: The cables or wireless channels used to transfer data in a network.
questions.explanation: Transmission media includes cables such as copper or fibre optic, and wireless methods such as radio waves.
